## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
With PrognosticEDMFX the grid cloud fraction was

    CF = a⁰ CF_env(q_c⁰) + Σⱼ aʲ 1[q_cʲ > 0],

the environment closure on the environment condensate weighted by the environment area, plus each updraft counted fully cloudy over its area wherever it carried any condensate. The binary updraft term has no lower bound on the in-cloud condensate: in coarse AMIP runs the surface-layer updrafts (area ~10 %, 0.01–0.03 g/kg of liquid in 30-m layers, τ ≲ 0.5 over the column) reported 10–13 % cover at 975–1000 hPa where ERA5 has 2–4 %, which under max-random overlap added ~6 pp to the total cloud cover.

The QuadratureCloud cover is now a single-domain quantity,

    CF = CF_env(a⁰ q_c⁰ + Σⱼ aʲ q_cʲ),

the environment PDF inversion applied to the grid-mean cloud condensate, with no area weighting and no updraft term. The microphysics quadrature is unchanged: the Lagrange multiplier is still fitted to the environment condensate, so the node condensate remains conserved exactly under the quadrature measure.

This changes cloud cover but doesn't affect radiation much. It makes ITCZ cloud cover better but Southern Ocean worse. The major problem of Southern Ocean is still in cloud condensate. I did try adding a threshold for updraft 1 or 0 cloud, and it can improve cloud fraction, but it introduces another ad hoc parameter, and I like this method better as it is more physical. I think cloud fraction will be improved once updraft fraction is taken into account as a skewness, and I will look into that next.

Also changes the default ice formation to TemperatureDependentIceNumber

Also changes the default of cloud_fraction_floor_residual to 1 so no release is used in cloud fraction. It's not important now. I will remove the release if I confirm it is not helpful in the end.
